claims.text: The proposed intervention is adding approximately 2–5 at.% Al to a refractory HEA.
Adding 2–5 at.% Al will promote in situ formation of an Al2O3 surface scale.
The resulting Al2O3 scale will be dense, continuous, and adherent.
Al preferentially oxidizes at high temperature to form Al2O3.
The Al2O3 layer will be slow-growing.
The Al2O3 scale will act as an oxygen-diffusion barrier.
The diffusion barrier will reduce oxygen ingress into the refractory HEA substrate.
Reduced oxygen ingress will retard oxidation kinetics and protect the underlying alloy microstructure.
At 1200°C in air for 100 hours, the Al-doped alloy will have lower oxidation weight gain than the untreated alloy.
At 1200°C in air for 100 hours, the Al-doped alloy will develop a thinner oxide scale than the untreated alloy.
The oxidation weight gain is anticipated to decrease by roughly 30% or more relative to the untreated alloy.
The proposed protective mechanism is expected to operate in high-temperature air at approximately 1000–1300°C.
Competing oxidation reactions may limit formation or effectiveness of the protective scale.
Scale spallation under thermal cycling may limit the intervention's effectiveness.

The hypothesis is to be rejected if the Al-doped alloy shows less than approximately a 30% reduction in oxidation weight gain or fails to form a continuous protective Al2O3 scale under the specified test conditions.
